chord-progression-generator.assumptionNote: Progressions are built only from diatonic chords (the seven chords native to the key). Borrowed chords, secondary dominants, and modulations are not included - they are advanced colours, not beginner foundations.
benefits: Break writer's block instantly with proven progressions in any key.
Hear every progression played back as real chords, not just names on a page.
Learn which chords belong to each key with the built-in diatonic reference.
Style presets (pop, rock, jazz, folk) teach you what makes each genre's harmony tick.

faqs.a: Roman numerals name scale degrees: I is the home chord (tonic), V pulls strongly back to I, and vi is the relative minor. Uppercase means major (IV, V), lowercase means minor (ii, vi), and the degree sign marks diminished (vii°). So I-V-vi-IV in C is C-G-Am-F.
faqs.q: What do the Roman numerals mean?

faqs.a: It is the most-used progression in modern pop: I-V-vi-IV. In C major that is C-G-Am-F; in G major it is G-D-Em-C. Hundreds of hit songs use exactly this loop because the V-vi move creates gentle tension and the IV-V lift resolves it.
faqs.q: What is the most common chord progression?

faqs.a: Start on the tonic (I or i) - it is home base. Then move to IV or V for lift, or vi for emotion. End phrases on V if you want tension, or I if you want rest. The generator's presets follow these instincts; study a few and you will feel the patterns.
faqs.q: How do I choose what comes next in a progression?

faqs.a: In a major key: I, ii, iii, IV, V, vi, vii° - for C major: C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am, Bdim. In a natural minor key: i, ii°, III, iv, v, VI, VII - for A minor: Am, Bdim, C, Dm, Em, F, G.
faqs.q: Which chords belong to each key?

faqs.a: Yes, in the random style. It picks diatonic chords with sensible weights and always starts on the tonic. Random does not mean chaotic here - every chord still belongs to the key, so it will always sound coherent.
faqs.q: Can it generate a truly random progression?

faqs.a: A progression is the order of chords; a key is the home note and scale everything is built from; a mode is which flavour of scale (major = bright, minor = dark). So C-G-Am-F is a progression in the key of C major, in the major mode.
faqs.q: What is the difference between a progression, a key, and a mode?

chord-progression-generator.formula:
Major key diatonic chords: I - ii - iii - IV - V - vi - vii°
Scale offsets (semitones): 0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11
Qualities: maj, min, min, maj, maj, min, dim
Natural minor: i - ii° - III - iv - v - VI - VII
Offsets: 0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10.
howTo: Pick your key: any of the 12 notes.
Choose major for a bright sound or minor for a darker one.
Pick a style preset - pop, rock, jazz, folk - or random for a surprise.
Choose 4 or 8 chords, then tap Generate for a fresh progression.
Tap Play to hear it, and check the diatonic reference to understand why it works.
keyFacts: A major key contains seven diatonic chords: I, ii, iii, IV, V, vi, vii° (e.g. C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am, Bdim in C major).
A natural minor key gives: i, ii°, III, iv, v, VI, VII (e.g. Am, Bdim, C, Dm, Em, F, G in A minor).
The V chord pulls hardest toward I - that tension-and-release is the engine of Western harmony.
I-V-vi-IV is the most-used pop progression of the last 30 years.
Every relative minor shares its major's chords: A minor uses exactly the chords of C major.
Starting and ending on the tonic (I or i) makes a progression feel like home.

limitations: Diatonic chords only - no borrowed chords, secondary dominants, or key changes.

Random mode is weighted toward common degrees, so truly unusual progressions are rare.
Chord names use sharps only; flat spellings are not shown.

chord-progression-generator.workedExample:
Generating a pop progression in C major:
1. Key = C, mode = major, style = pop, length = 4.
2. The generator picks the classic pattern I - V - vi - IV.
3. Degrees to chords: I = C (offset 0), V = G (offset 7), vi = Am (offset 9, minor), IV = F (offset 5).
4. Result: C - G - Am - F.
5. Tap Play: you hear four triads - C-E-G, G-B-D, A-C-E, F-A-C - the backbone of hundreds of hit songs.
